anomaly_def.Name: Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly: Sustained physical-device bandwidth and latency limits are reached, so every read or write request queues and waits.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly: Physical or logical free space on data, log, temp, or backup volumes is exhausted or about to exhaust, preventing further allocations.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly: The network path, listener, or connection-handling layer cannot accept, transmit, or maintain the required number of client sessions or bytes in flight.

When all three exist simultaneously, the database shows a volatile mix of symptoms: I/O wait events soar while read/write latencies fluctuate; auto-extension, log switch, temp usage, or backup operations intermittently fail with out-of-space errors; connection establishment and result-set delivery stall or time out, and clients see both "no space" and "cannot connect" errors. Backend processes may accumulate in client-read/client-write and buffer-I/O waits at once, queue depths on storage devices remain full, and network socket queues overflow, making it difficult to attribute the primary bottleneck. Batch windows elongate, checkpoints linger, archiving falls behind, and retry storms from the application add further load across all three constrained resources.

Causally, the three root causes amplify one another: slow storage throughput lengthens the time each write holds file handles and network sockets, pushing up concurrent session counts and exhausting listener backlogs. At the same time, reduced throughput delays log archival and backup jobs, accelerating space consumption until capacity thresholds are hit, which in turn forces additional synchronous space checks and allocation overhead that further degrades I/O performance. Network congestion or connection thrashing slows remote copy or replication traffic, preventing space-reclaim operations and keeping disks fuller for longer, while client retries multiply transactional I/O and network chatter. The feedback loop among limited bandwidth, shrinking space, and choking connectivity drives the database into a compounded degradation state that is more severe than any single anomaly alone.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
